question: The part VII of the Indian constitution has been omitted. It is related with which of the following?

options.text: States in part B of the first schedule
Armed forces in states in part A of the second schedule
Reservation for Anglo –Indian communities in parliament

solution:
Correct Answer **States in part B of the first schedule**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Out of the 22 parts of the Indian Constitution that originally existed during its formation, the only part which has been deleted is Part VII.
 
• It was repealed by the Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1956.
 
• It dealt with the Part-B States in the Indian Union.
 
 
• At the time of Independence and during the framing of the Constitution, India consisted of three types of states. A, B and C
 
• The Part B states were former princely states or groups of princely states.
 
• The Part B states were Hyderabad, Jammu & Kashmir, Madhya Bharat, Mysore, Patiala, East Punjab States Union (Pepsu), Rajasthan, Saurashtra, and Travancore-Cochin.
 
• When all the states were reorganized on a linguistic basis through the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act was also passed.
 
• This completely led to a permanent alteration of the Indian Map and very much near to the present one. Hence Part B states were completely removed.
 
• The scheme of Part A, B, and C states were completely done away with and the only classification that now remains is States and the Union Territories.
 
• Hence the Seventh Amendment deleted Part VII which dealt with Part B states now stands omitted.
